George Clooney Questions Government AI Regulation
Speaking at a Venice Film Festival symposium on the future of creativity, Clooney said he was wary of putting AI regulation entirely in the hands of government officials, Variety reported on Friday.

He said, "I don’t know that you want government to be regulating this either, because I sit and watch when Zuckerberg is testifying in front of, you know, a 94-year-old Chuck Grassley, and they’re like, ‘Well, how do you turn that computer on?’"
"These are not the people that you want to entrust the holy grail with," he said.

children: Clooney Warns AI Could Make Truth Harder to Find
Clooney’s concerns extend beyond AI-generated misinformation. He argued that increasingly convincing AI content could make people question whether real events ever happened.
"It’s not just that you’ll see lies," he said. "It also makes you question things that really do exist."
He warned that AI could give false claims and established facts similar weight, potentially making it harder for people to distinguish historical truth from fabricated narratives.
